bull.b: Sustained multi-year revenue growth and large margin expansion reflect durable operating leverage and a higher-value product mix across aerospace and industrial businesses. These trends indicate improved pricing, scale advantages, and structural profitability that should persist as long as build rates and spares demand remain healthy.

Robust operating cash flow and consistently high free cash flow provide long-term financial flexibility to fund capex, buybacks, dividends, and deleveraging. The strengthened balance sheet reduces financial risk and increases optionality for strategic investments and capital returns over the next several quarters.

Exceptional demand in gas turbines and a sizable spares business create recurring, higher-margin revenue streams that are less cyclical than new-build volumes. A strong aftermarket mix and widening adoption for industrial applications support steady revenue visibility and pricing power over medium-term cycles.

bear.b: A multi-year increase in required capital spending to expand aerospace and IGT capacity raises execution risk and reduces near-term free-cash-flow conversion. Higher capex extends payback timelines and increases sensitivity to demand shocks while capacity comes online over several years.

Acquisition-related integration (IT, supply chain, harmonization) and debt servicing compress consolidated margins and delay realization of expected synergies. This creates medium-term execution risk where consolidation costs and timing could offset organic gains through the end of the synergy horizon.

bear.t: Commodity pass-through and volume pressure in Forged Wheels
bear.b: Exposure to raw-material pass-throughs and cyclical transportation volumes produces margin volatility in Forged Wheels. Persistent commodity-driven margin dilution and volume sensitivity can weigh on consolidated profitability until price resets or volume recovery stabilizes.
